design: paired item-by-item: same 175 deterministic residuals run under A2 (guided: Lean verdict given) and A1 (blind: verdict self-decided). Same solver residual set, same judge (commit 6805e232, DEFAULT_PROOF_POLICY). Follows the FiberRing A1/A2 cue-conditioning methodology.
finding: No measurable cost of blindness: guided and blind are statistically indistinguishable (172 both; 3 disagreements split 1 guided-only / 2 blind-only; net gap -1 of 175). The Lean-verdict cue (A2) does not improve solve rate over blind (A1), because the counterexample/proof search itself reveals the verdict.
caveat: Both conditions saturate near ceiling (173-174/175 ~= 99%), so this paired design cannot resolve a small cue effect; the 3 differing items are within codex run-to-run stochasticity (6-8 attempts each), not a demonstrated systematic effect. A harder or larger item pool where neither condition saturates is needed to measure a non-trivial gap.
note_vs_fiberring: FiberRing A1/A2 measures routing-to-proof-template accuracy; this measures solve-rate under the same cue-conditioning contrast (verdict cue vs none). Related axis, different dependent variable.
